# Gate levels

`project.toml [gates] level` is one of three values. Explain them to the founder in these
words, not in your own; a level is what this file says it is.

## Never relaxed, at any level

- Outward steps (deploy, merge, push, publish, send, pay, delete, real data writes) wait for the
  founder's go, one step at a time (`skills/ordered-steps/`).
- Data writes prove themselves and can be undone (`skills/safe-data-write/`).
- The commit-msg hook refuses banned characters (`skills/commit/`).
- No unconfirmed assumptions (rule 10), and every rejected idea is recorded (rule 12).
- Free tiers are strict, with tested caps before release.

## What changes

| | strict | standard | light |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requirement row before a change | always, new or cited | always for features; a copy or style fix cites the row of the screen it touches | one row per prototype area, cited in every commit; detail optional |
| Grilling and readiness gate | every feature | every feature | none |
| Spec audit (`skills/spec-audit/`) | every feature | features touching existing code | none |
| Security and legal review | every feature touching data, money, AI output or claims | only where the feature's spec flags them | before any real user or real data |
| Full sweep | before every hand-off and every commit | before every commit | before every commit |
| QA report | every change | every feature | before any real user |

**Light is for throwaway prototypes only:** no real users, no real personal data, no payments.
Moving from light to anything else means writing the missing requirement rows first.

## Recommending

Setup always recommends strict and says what it buys, using the table above. If the founder
chooses another level, record the level, the reason and when to revisit it in
`p1-closed-decisions.md`, and the declined recommendation in `p1-rejected.md`.
